title: EFSA assesses safety of green tea catechins | EFSA
abstract: # EFSA assesses safety of green tea catechins. **EFSA has assessed the safety of green tea catechins from dietary sources, following concerns regarding their possible harmful effects on the liver. EFSA concluded that catechins from green tea infusions and similar drinks are generally safe. EFSA’s assessment of green tea catechins was triggered by concerns from Nordic countries following reported cases of liver damage possibly associated with the use of green tea products. In its safety assessment, EFSA looked at possible links between the consumption of EGCG in green tea infusions and food supplements and liver damage. Food supplements containing green tea catechins provide a daily EGCG intakeThe amount of a substance (e.g. nutrient or chemical) that is ingested by a person or animal via the diet ranging from 5-1000 mg. Experts also proposed clearer labelling of green tea products (in particular food supplements) regarding catechin content and their possible health risks.
